docs.title: pyjelly
docs.text: pyjelly is a Python implementation of Jelly, a high-performance binary serialization format and streaming protocol for RDF knowledge graphs. It works great with RDFLib and also without any extra libraries.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fast reading and writing of RDF knowledge graphs in the Jelly format
  • Seamless integration with RDFLib
  • Stream processing support for large datasets or streams of many RDF graphs/datasets

  • Overview and supported features
  • Generic interface (usage without RDFLib)

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
pyjelly is compatible with Python 3.10 and newer. Python 3.10–3.14 are tested in CI and are guaranteed to work.

The following table shows the compatibility of the pyjelly implementation with other libraries:

pyjelly Python RDFLib 0.7.0 – 0.8.2 3.10 – 3.14 7.x (>= 7.1.4) 0.1.0 – 0.6.2 3.9 – 3.13 7.x (>= 7.1.4)

See the release notes on GitHub for more details.

docs.title: Commercial and community support
docs.text:
NeverBlink provides commercial support services for Jelly, including implementing custom features, system integrations, implementations for new frameworks, benchmarking, and more.

Community support is available on the Jelly Discord chat.

def parse_triples_stream(
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame],
    options: ParserOptions,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
) -> Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
    """
    Parse flat triple stream.

    Args:
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]): iterator over stream frames
        options (ParserOptions): stream options
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
                used for extracting frame metadata

    Yields:
        Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
            Generator of iterables of Triple or Prefix objects,
            one iterable per frame.

    """
    adapter = GenericTriplesAdapter(options)
    decoder = Decoder(adapter=adapter)
    for frame in frames:
        if frame_metadata is not None:
            frame_metadata.set(
                frame.metadata
            ) if frame.metadata else frame_metadata.set({})
        yield decoder.iter_rows(frame)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        yield decoder.end_of_stream()

def parse_quads_stream(
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame],
    options: ParserOptions,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
) -> Generator[Iterable[Quad | Prefix]]:
    """
    Parse flat quads stream.

    Args:
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]): iterator over stream frames
        options (ParserOptions): stream options
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
                used for extracting frame metadata

    Yields:
        Generator[Iterable[Quad | Prefix]]:
            Generator of iterables of Quad or Prefix objects,
            one iterable per frame.

    """
    adapter_class: type[GenericQuadsBaseAdapter]
    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS:
        adapter_class = GenericQuadsAdapter
    else:
        adapter_class = GenericGraphsAdapter
    adapter = adapter_class(options=options)
    decoder = Decoder(adapter=adapter)
    for frame in frames:
        if frame_metadata is not None:
            frame_metadata.set(
                frame.metadata
            ) if frame.metadata else frame_metadata.set({})
        yield decoder.iter_rows(frame)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        yield decoder.end_of_stream()

    Yields:
        Generator[GenericStatementSink]:
            returns generators for GenericStatementSink, regardless of stream type.

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (
        st is None
        or st.logical_type == jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
        or st.flat
    ):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )

        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected GROUPED logical type, got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        for graph in grouped_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(
                frames=frames, options=options, frame_metadata=frame_metadata
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = sink_factory()
            for graph_item in graph:
                if isinstance(graph_item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(graph_item.prefix, graph_item.iri)
                else:
                    sink.add(graph_item)
            yield sink
        return
    elif options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        for dataset in grouped_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(
                frames=frames, options=options, frame_metadata=frame_metadata
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = sink_factory()
            for item in dataset:
                if isinstance(item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)
                else:
                    sink.add(item)
            yield sink
        return

    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def parse_jelly_flat(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame] | None = None,
    options: ParserOptions | None = None,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Statement | Prefix]:  # type: ignore[valid-type, unused-ignore]
    """
    Parse jelly file with FLAT logical type into a Generator of stream events.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream.
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None):
            jelly frames if read before.
        options (ParserOptions | None): stream options
            if read before.
        logical_type_strict (bool): If True, validate the *logical* type
            in stream options and require FLAT (TRIPLES/QUADS).
            Otherwise, only the physical type is used to route parsing.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if physical type is not supported

    Yields:
        Generator[Statement | Prefix]: Generator of stream events

    """
    if frames is None or options is None:
        options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (st is None or not st.flat):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )

        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected FLAT logical type (TRIPLES/QUADS), got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(frames=frames, options=options), options
        )
        return
    if options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(frames=frames, options=options), options
        )
        return
    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def triples_stream_frames(
    stream: TripleStream,
    data: GenericStatementSink | Generator[Triple],
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a GenericStatementSink into frames using physical type triples stream.

    Args:
        stream (TripleStream): stream that specifies triples processing
        data (GenericStatementSink | Generator[Triple]):
            GenericStatementSink/Statements to serialize.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: jelly frames.

    stream.enroll()
    if (
        isinstance(data, GenericStatementSink)
        and stream.options.params.namespace_declarations
    ):
        yield from namespace_declarations(data, stream)

    graphs = (data,)
    for graph in graphs:
        for terms in graph:
            if frame := stream.triple(terms):
                yield frame
        if frame := stream.flow.frame_from_graph():
            yield frame
    if stream.stream_types.flat and (frame := stream.flow.to_stream_frame()):
        yield frame

def guess_options(
    sink: GenericStatementSink, *, grouped: bool = False
) -> SerializerOptions:
    """
    Guess the serializer options based on the store type.

    For a stream of graphs or datasets (`grouped`), each is an RDF Message in
    Jelly-RDF 1.2, and one frame in Jelly-RDF 1.1.
    """
    if sink.is_triples_sink:
        logical_type = (
            jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS
            if grouped
            else jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES
        )
    else:
        logical_type = (
            jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_DATASETS
            if grouped
            else jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_QUADS
        )
    # Generic sink supports both RDF-star and generalized statements by default
    # as it can handle any term types including quoted triples and generalized RDF terms
    params = StreamParameters(generalized_statements=True, rdf_star=True)
    return SerializerOptions(logical_type=logical_type, params=params)

def guess_stream(options: SerializerOptions, sink: GenericStatementSink) -> Stream:
    """
    Return an appropriate stream implementation for the given options.

    Notes: if base(!) logical type is GRAPHS and sink.is_triples_sink is false,

    stream_cls: type[Stream]

        stream_cls = QuadStream
    else:
        stream_cls = TripleStream

        options=options,
    )

    sink_generator: Generator[GenericStatementSink],

) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:

    Transform multiple GenericStatementSinks into Jelly frames.

            stream = guess_stream(options, sink)
        yield from stream_frames(stream, sink)

def flat_stream_to_frames(
    statements: Generator[Triple | Quad],
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a stream of raw GenericStatementSink's triples or quads into Jelly frames.

    Args:
        statements (Generator[Triple | Quad]):
          s/p/o triples or s/p/o/g quads to serialize.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional):
            if omitted, guessed based on the first tuple.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: generated frames.

    """
    first = next(statements, None)
    if first is None:
        return

    sink = GenericStatementSink()
    sink.add(first)
    if options is None:
        options = guess_options(sink)
    stream = guess_stream(options, sink)

    combined: Generator[Triple | Quad] | GenericStatementSink = (
        item for item in chain([first], statements)
    )

    yield from stream_frames(stream, combined)

def parse_triples_stream(
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame],
    options: ParserOptions,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
    *,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
    """
    Parse flat triple stream.

    Args:
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]): iterator over stream frames
        options (ParserOptions): stream options
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
            used for extracting frame metadata
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Yields:
        Generator[Iterable[Triple | Prefix]]:
            Generator of iterables of Triple or Prefix objects,
            one iterable per frame.

    """
    adapter = RDFLibTriplesAdapter(options, validate_iris=validate_iris)
    decoder = Decoder(adapter=adapter)
    for frame in frames:
        if frame_metadata is not None:
            frame_metadata.set(
                frame.metadata
            ) if frame.metadata else frame_metadata.set({})
        yield decoder.iter_rows(frame)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        yield decoder.end_of_stream()

def parse_jelly_grouped(  # noqa: PLR0913 keyword-only options
    inp: IO[bytes],
    graph_factory: Callable[[], Graph] = Graph,
    dataset_factory: Callable[[], Dataset] = Dataset,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
    frame_metadata: ContextVar[MutableMapping[str, bytes]] | None = None,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Graph] | Generator[Dataset]:
    """
    Take jelly file and return generators based on the detected physical type.

    Yields one graph/dataset per frame.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream
        graph_factory (Callable): lambda to construct a Graph.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Graph,
            but you can pass something else here.
        dataset_factory (Callable): lambda to construct a Dataset.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Dataset,
            but you can pass something else here.
        logical_type_strict (bool): If True, validate the *logical* type in
            stream options and require a grouped logical type. Otherwise, only the
            physical type is used to route parsing.
        frame_metadata: (ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]]): context variable
            used for extracting frame metadata
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: is raised if a physical type is not implemented

    Yields:
        Generator[Graph] | Generator[Dataset]:
            returns generators for graphs/datasets based on the type of input

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    st = getattr(options, "stream_types", None)
    if logical_type_strict and (
        st is None
        or st.logical_type == jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
        or st.flat
    ):
        lt_name = (
            "UNSPECIFIED"
            if st is None
            else jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(st.logical_type)
        )

        msg = (
            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected GROUPED logical type, got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        for graph in grouped_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(
                frames=frames,
                options=options,
                frame_metadata=frame_metadata,
                validate_iris=validate_iris,
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = graph_factory()
            for graph_item in graph:
                if isinstance(graph_item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(graph_item.prefix, graph_item.iri)
                else:
                    sink.add(graph_item)
            yield sink
        return
    elif options.stream_types.physical_type in (
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
    ):
        for dataset in grouped_rows(
            parse_quads_stream(
                frames=frames,
                options=options,
                frame_metadata=frame_metadata,
                validate_iris=validate_iris,
            ),
            options,
        ):
            sink = dataset_factory()
            for item in dataset:
                if isinstance(item, Prefix):
                    sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)
                else:
                    s, p, o, graph_name = item
                    context = sink.get_context(graph_name)
                    sink.add((s, p, o, context))
            yield sink
        return

    physical_type_name = jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(
        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def parse_jelly_to_graph(
    inp: IO[bytes],
    graph_factory: Callable[[], Graph] = Graph,
    dataset_factory: Callable[[], Dataset] = Dataset,
    *,
    validate_iris: bool = False,
) -> Graph | Dataset:
    """
    Add statements from Generator to provided Graph/Dataset.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly stream.
        graph_factory (Callable[[], Graph]): factory to create Graph.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Graph,
            but you can pass something else here.
        dataset_factory (Callable[[], Dataset]): factory to create Dataset.
            By default creates an empty in-memory Dataset,
            but you can pass something else here.
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Returns:
        Dataset | Graph: Dataset or Graph with statements.

    """
    options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

    sink: Graph
    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        sink = graph_factory()
        # Graph.add only checks the terms before giving them to the store
        to_store = type(sink).add is Graph.add
    else:
        # Other stream types fail in parse_jelly_flat
        sink = dataset_factory()
        # Dataset.add would also make a new context graph for every quad
        to_store = type(sink).add is ConjunctiveGraph.add

    items = parse_jelly_flat(
        inp=inp, frames=frames, options=options, validate_iris=validate_iris
    )
    if to_store:
        _add_to_store(sink, items)
        return sink

    # The Graph or Dataset class changes add(), so it gets every statement
    for item in items:
        if isinstance(item, Prefix):
            sink.bind(item.prefix, item.iri)
        if isinstance(item, Triple):
            sink.add(item)
        if isinstance(item, Quad):
            s, p, o, graph_name = item
            context = cast(Dataset, sink).get_context(graph_name)
            sink.add((s, p, o, context))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return sink

    inp: IO[bytes],
    frames: Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame] | None = None,
    options: ParserOptions | None = None,
    *,
    logical_type_strict: bool = False,
    validate_iris: bool = False,

    Parse jelly file with FLAT logical type into a Generator of stream events.

    Args:
        inp (IO[bytes]): input jelly buffered binary stream.
        frames (Iterable[jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None):
            jelly frames if read before.

            if read before.

            physical type is used to route parsing.
        validate_iris (bool): whether rdflib checks the IRIs. An invalid IRI is
            still read, rdflib only logs a warning. Checking slows down parsing.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if physical type is not supported

    Yields:

        options, frames = get_options_and_frames(inp)

            "strict logical type check requires options.stream_types"
            if st is None
            else f"expected FLAT logical type (TRIPLES/QUADS), got {lt_name}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if options.stream_types.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_TRIPLES:
        yield from flat_rows(
            parse_triples_stream(
                frames=frames, options=options, validate_iris=validate_iris

        jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,

            parse_quads_stream(frames=frames, options=options), options

        options.stream_types.physical_type
    )
    msg = f"the stream type {physical_type_name} is not supported "
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def serialize(  # type: ignore[override]
    self,
    out: IO[bytes],
    /,
    *,
    stream: Stream | None = None,
    options: SerializerOptions | None = None,
    **unused: Any,
) -> None:
    """
    Serialize self.store content to Jelly format.

    Args:
        out (IO[bytes]): output buffered writer
        stream (Stream | None, optional): Jelly stream object. Defaults to None.
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional): Serializer options
            if defined beforehand, e.g., read from a separate file.
            Defaults to None.
        **unused(Any): unused args for RDFLib serialize

    """
    if options is None:
        options = guess_options(self.store)
    if stream is None:
        stream = guess_stream(options, self.store)
    frames = stream_frames(stream, self.store)
    if stream.options.params.delimited:
        for stream_frame in frames:
            write_delimited(stream_frame, out)
        return
    written = False
    for stream_frame in frames:
        if written:
            msg = (
                "the data does not fit in one frame. A non-delimited stream can "
                "only have one frame. Write a delimited stream, or use larger "
                "lookups."
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        write_single(stream_frame, out)
        written = True

@stream_frames.register(TripleStream)
def triples_stream_frames(
    stream: TripleStream,
    data: Graph | Dataset | Iterable[Triple],
) -> Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Serialize a Graph/Dataset into jelly frames.

    Args:
        stream (TripleStream): stream that specifies triples processing
        data (Graph | Dataset | Iterable[Triple]):
            Graph/Dataset/Statements to serialize.

    Notes:
        if Dataset is given, its graphs are unpacked and iterated over
        if flow is GraphsFrameFlow, emits a frame per graph.

    Yields:
        Generator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]: jelly frames.

    """
    stream.enroll()
    if isinstance(data, Graph) and stream.options.params.namespace_declarations:
        yield from namespace_declarations(data, stream)

    graphs = (data,) if not isinstance(data, Dataset) else data.graphs()
    for graph in graphs:
        tree = spo_tree(graph) if isinstance(graph, Graph) else None
        if tree is not None:
            # An in-memory graph, grouped by subject and predicate
            yield from write_tree(stream, tree)
        else:
            # Any other store, or a generator of triples, in its own order
            yield from stream.triples(graph)
        if frame := stream.flow.frame_from_graph():
            yield frame
    if stream.stream_types.flat and (frame := stream.flow.to_stream_frame()):
        yield frame

    2

    4

def spo_tree(graph: Graph) -> Tree | None:
    """
    Return the graph's triples as a subject -> predicate -> objects tree.

    Only for rdflib's in-memory store, whose triples are in memory anyway. For any
    other store, return None: such a store can be far too big to group in memory.
    Its triples are then written in the store's own order, which for stores with
    indexes (e.g., Oxigraph, BerkeleyDB) is usually already grouped by subject.
    """
    store = graph.store
    if type(store) is not Memory:
        return None
    indexes = _memory_indexes(store)
    if indexes is None:
        # The private fields are not there: group with the public API
        return _group(graph.triples((None, None, None)))
    contexts = indexes.context_triples
    context = indexes.context_key(graph)
    triples = contexts.get(context)
    if not triples:
        return {}
    if not any(key not in (None, context) and value for key, value in contexts.items()):
        # The graph is alone in its store, so the store's subject-predicate-object
        # index contains its triples, already grouped and in the order they
        # were added
        return indexes.spo
    return _group(triples)

Uses the stream's cursor API, so the stream doesn't compare terms. In a tree, each subject differs from the one before it, and so do the predicates of one subject and the objects of one predicate. def write_tree(stream: Stream, tree: Tree) -> Iterator[jelly.RdfStreamFrame]:
    """
    Write the statements of a subject -> predicate -> objects tree.

    Uses the stream's cursor API, so the stream doesn't compare terms. In a tree,
    each subject differs from the one before it, and so do the predicates of one
    subject and the objects of one predicate. Only the first subject of the tree
    and the first predicate of a subject can be equal to the one before it (e.g.,
    rdf:type as the first predicate of every subject), so only those are
    compared. The first object of a predicate is rarely equal to the object
    before it, and most predicates have only one object, so objects are not
    compared: an equal one is just written again.

    Yields:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame: full frames.

    """
    encoder = stream.encoder
    terms = stream.repeated_terms
    first_subject = True
    for s, predicates in tree.items():
        if not first_subject or not encoder.same_term(terms[0], s):
            stream.set_subject(s)
        first_subject = False
        first_predicate = True
        for p, objects in predicates.items():
            if not first_predicate or not encoder.same_term(terms[1], p):
                stream.set_predicate(p)
            first_predicate = False
            for o in objects:
                stream.set_object(o)
                frame = stream.emit()
                if frame is not None:
                    yield frame

    stream: QuadStream, trees: Iterable[tuple[Any, Tree]]

def iter_frame(self, frame: jelly.RdfStreamFrame) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """
    Return the namespace declarations and statements of a frame.

    The stream options and the lookup entries of the frame are read right away,
    the statements as they are iterated.
    """
    message_ended = False
    rows = frame.rows
    if rows:
        if len(rows) > 1 or _ROW_WHICH_ONEOF(rows[0], "row") != "options":
            msg = (
                "a frame of a Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream can only have the stream "
                "options in its rows, in one row"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if self.options_read:
            message_ended = self.restate_options(rows[0].options)
        else:
            self.options_read = True
    if not _FRAME_HAS_FIELD(frame, "columns"):
        return iter((MESSAGE_END,) if message_ended else ())
    if not self.options_read:
        msg = "the stream has statements before the stream options"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    batch_rows = self.iter_batch(frame.columns)
    if message_ended:

def restate_options(self, options: jelly.RdfStreamOptions) -> bool:
    """
    Read restated stream options, which empty the lookups.

    Returns:
        bool: whether an RDF Message ended, because it had statements.

    """
    current = self.decoder.options
    if (
        options.version != current.params.version
        or options.physical_type != current.stream_types.physical_type
        or options.stream_type != current.params.stream_type

            "in all stream options of a stream"

def iter_batch(self, batch: jelly.RdfColumnBatch) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """Return the namespace declarations and statements of a batch."""
    rows = batch.row_count
    if rows > MAX_ROWS:
        msg = f"a frame can have at most {MAX_ROWS} statements, not {rows}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    lengths = self.message_lengths(batch, rows)
    # All lookup entries come first, so that the columns can refer to them
    self.ingest_entries(batch)
    namespaces = self.namespaces(batch) if batch.namespaces else []
    has_graphs = _BATCH_HAS_FIELD(batch, "graphs")
    if has_graphs and not self.quads:
        msg = "a stream of triples cannot have a graphs column"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    subjects = self.runs(batch.subjects, rows, _RESOURCES, "subject")
    predicates = self.runs(batch.predicates, rows, _IRIS, "predicate")
    objects = self.runs(batch.objects, rows, _ANY, "object")
    graphs = None
    if self.quads:
        if has_graphs:
            graphs = self.runs(batch.graphs, rows, _RESOURCES, "graph")
        else:
            graphs = _Runs([], rows, "graph")
            graphs.add(None, rows)
        graphs.set_unbound(self.decoder.adapter.default_graph())

    # The statements of each RDF Message that ends in the batch, and the rest

def statements(
    self,
    counts: list[int],
    subjects: _Runs,
    predicates: _Runs,
    objects: _Runs,
    graphs: _Runs | None,
) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """Yield the statements, `counts` at a time, with MESSAGE_END in between."""
    adapter = self.decoder.adapter
    last = len(counts) - 1
    for i, count in enumerate(counts):
        if graphs is None:
            for _ in range(count):
                yield adapter.triple(
                    (subjects.next(), predicates.next(), objects.next())
                )
        else:
            for _ in range(count):
                yield adapter.quad(
                    (
                        subjects.next(),
                        predicates.next(),
                        objects.next(),
                        graphs.next(),
                    )
                )
        if i < last:
            yield MESSAGE_END

def runs(
    self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, rows: int, allowed: int, position: str
) -> _Runs:
    """Decode a column into its runs, whose cells add up to the row count."""
    values = self.run_values(column, allowed, position)
    unbound_allowed = position == "graph"
    layouts: list[int] = column.layouts[:]
    runs = _Runs(values, rows, position)
    index = 0
    k = 0
    while k < len(layouts):
        token = layouts[k]
        k += 1
        length = token & _LENGTH_MASK
        if length == _LENGTH_MASK:
            if k == len(layouts):
                msg = (
                    f"corrupt layout of the {position} column: a length is cut off"
                )
                raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
            length += layouts[k]
            k += 1
        skip = token >> _SKIP_SHIFT
        if index + skip > len(values):
            msg = (
                f"corrupt layout of the {position} column: it skips past its values"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        runs.add_values(index, skip)
        index += skip
        if token & _UNBOUND:
            if not unbound_allowed:
                raise _unbound(position)
            runs.add(None, length + 1)
        elif index < len(values):
            runs.add(values[index], length + 2)
            index += 1
        else:
            msg = (
                f"corrupt layout of the {position} column: a repeated value is "
                "past its values"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    runs.add_values(index, len(values) - index)
    if runs.cells < rows:
        if not unbound_allowed:
            raise _unbound(position)
        runs.add(None, rows - runs.cells)
    return runs

def run_values(
    self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, allowed: int, position: str
) -> list[Any]:
    """Decode the run values of a column, in order."""

        len(column.name_ids),
        len(column.lex_values),
        len(column.bnodes),
        len(column.triple_terms),

        if counts[kind] and not allowed & (1 << kind):
            msg = f"the {position} column cannot have {_KIND_NAMES[kind]}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

    if sum(1 for count in counts if count) > 1:
        msg = f"the {position} column has terms of more than one type, but no kinds"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)

        return self.literals(column)
    if counts[_KIND_BNODE]:
        return self.bnodes(column)
    if counts[_KIND_TRIPLE]:
        return self.triple_terms(column)
    return self.iris(column)

def mixed_values(
    self, column: jelly.RdfColumn, counts: tuple[int, ...], position: str
) -> list[Any]:
    """Decode the run values of a column whose kinds say which type each is."""
    kinds: bytes = column.kinds
    value_count = sum(counts)
    _check_kinds(kinds, value_count, position)
    iris = self.iris(column)
    literals = self.literals(column)
    bnodes = self.bnodes(column)
    triple_terms = self.triple_terms(column)
    # How many values of each type were taken. If no type runs out of values,
    # all are used up at the end, as there are value_count of them
    iri = literal = bnode = triple = 0
    values: list[Any] = []
    for i in range(value_count):
        kind = (kinds[i >> 2] >> ((i & 3) << 1)) & 3
        if kind == _KIND_IRI:
            if iri == len(iris):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(iris[iri])
            iri += 1
        elif kind == _KIND_LITERAL:
            if literal == len(literals):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(literals[literal])
            literal += 1
        elif kind == _KIND_BNODE:
            if bnode == len(bnodes):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(bnodes[bnode])
            bnode += 1
        else:
            if triple == len(triple_terms):
                raise _kinds_mismatch(position, kind)
            values.append(triple_terms[triple])
            triple += 1
    return values

def literal_kind(self, kind: int, langtags: Any, directions: Any) -> _LiteralKind:
    """Resolve a literal kind: its language tag, datatype and base direction."""
    decoder = self.decoder
    if not kind:
        return _LiteralKind(decoder, None, None, None)
    if kind & 1:
        datatype = decoder.datatypes.at((kind + 1) >> 1)
        return _LiteralKind(decoder, None, datatype, None)
    index = (kind >> 1) - 1
    if index >= len(langtags):
        msg = f"a literal kind refers to language tag {index}, which is not there"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    direction = None
    if directions and directions[index]:
        direction = self.direction(directions[index])
    return _LiteralKind(decoder, langtags[index] or None, None, direction)

def __init__(self, adapter: Adapter) -> None:
    """
    Initialize decoder.

    Initializes decoder with lookup tables of preset sizes and an
    integration-dependent adapter.

    Args:
        adapter (Adapter): integration-dependent adapter that specifies terms
        conversion to specific objects, framing,
        namespace declarations, and graphs/datasets forming.

    """
    self.adapter = adapter
    self.new_lookups()
    # The last s, p, o and g terms, for repeated terms
    self.repeated_terms: list[object] = [_MISSING] * 4
    # Literals often repeat (e.g., the same values in many entities), and
    # making one is often slow (rdflib parses the value). By language tag and
    # datatype, then by lexical form, see literal_cache()
    self.literal_caches: dict[tuple[str | None, str | None], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    self.literal_cache_size = 0

    self.term_handlers: dict[type[Any], TermHandler] = {
        t: getattr(self, name) for t, name in self._TERM_HANDLER_NAMES.items()
    }
    #: Decodes the frames of Jelly-RDF 1.2 streams, None for older ones
    self.column_decoder: ColumnDecoder | None = None
    if not is_row_layout(self.options.params.version):
        self.column_decoder = ColumnDecoder(self)

    """Yield the decoded rows of a frame of a Jelly-RDF 1.0 or 1.1 stream."""
    # Rows are told apart by the name of their field, most common ones first

        elif kind == "name":

        elif kind == "datatype":
            self.ingest_datatype_entry(row_owner.datatype)

def decode_iri(self, iri: jelly.RdfIri) -> Any:
    """
    Decode RdfIri message to IRI using a custom adapter.

    The term is reused if the same name and prefix entries were decoded
    before, so the adapter's IRI terms must be immutable.

    Args:
        iri (jelly.RdfIri): RdfIri message

    Returns:
        Any: IRI, based on adapter implementation, e.g., rdflib.term.URIRef

    names = self.names
    name_index = iri.name_id or names.last_reused_index + 1
    name = names.decode_name_term_index(name_index)
    prefix = self.prefixes.decode_prefix_term_index(iri.prefix_id)
    # The lookup tables keep the strings they were given, so the same objects
    # mean the same entries (or at least equal strings, which is just as good)
    cached = self.iri_cache[name_index]
    if cached is not None and cached.name is name and cached.prefix is prefix:
        return cached.term
    return self.new_iri(name_index, name, prefix)

def decode_statement(self, fields: list[Any], size: int) -> list[Any]:
    """
    Decode the terms of a triple or quad message.

    Notes: also updates the repeated terms

    Args:
        fields (list[Any]): the message's fields, from ListFields()
        size (int): 3 for a triple, 4 for a quad

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a missing repeated term is encountered

    Returns:
        Any: a list of decoded terms

    """
    repeated = self.repeated_terms
    terms = repeated[:size]
    # The fields come in the order of their numbers, so the terms are decoded
    # in s, p, o, g order. Each term has four fields, numbered from 1:
    # IRI, blank node, literal and quoted triple (s_iri = 1, ..., o_iri = 9),
    # but the graph's are IRI, blank node, default graph and literal
    for field, value in fields:
        number: int = field.number - 1
        position = number >> 2
        kind = number & 3
        if kind == _IRI:
            term = self.decode_iri(value)
        elif kind == _BNODE:
            term = self.adapter.bnode(value)
        elif kind == _LITERAL_OR_DEFAULT_GRAPH:
            if position == _GRAPH:
                term = self.adapter.default_graph()
            else:
                term = self.decode_literal(value)
        elif position == _GRAPH:
            term = self.decode_literal(value)
        else:
            term = self.decode_quoted_triple(value)
        terms[position] = term
        repeated[position] = term
    for i in range(size):
        if terms[i] is _MISSING:
            msg = f"missing repeated term {_POSITIONS[i]}"
            raise ValueError(msg)
    return terms

def check_stream_options(options: jelly.RdfStreamOptions) -> None:
    """
    Check that the parser can read a stream with these options.

    The fields of one layout must not be set in a stream of the
    other. The lookups must not be larger than the parser allows (see the
    MAX_*_LOOKUP_SIZE constants).

    Raises:
        JellyConformanceError: if it can't.

    """
    version = options.version
    if not MIN_VERSION <= version <= MAX_VERSION:
        msg = (
            f"unsupported protocol version {version}, "
            f"expected {MIN_VERSION} to {MAX_VERSION}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    physical_type = options.physical_type
    if physical_type not in _PHYSICAL_TYPES:
        msg = f"unknown physical stream type: {physical_type}"
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    if is_row_layout(version):
        if options.stream_type or options.rdf_version:
            msg = (
                "the stream type and RDF version are only valid in Jelly-RDF 1.2 "
                "streams (protocol version 3)"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if options.logical_type not in _LOGICAL_TYPES:
            msg = f"unknown logical stream type: {options.logical_type}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        min_names = MIN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE
    else:
        if options.generalized_statements or options.rdf_star or options.logical_type:
            msg = (
                "generalized statements, RDF-star and logical stream types are only "
                "valid in Jelly-RDF 1.0 and 1.1 streams (protocol versions 1 and 2)"
            )
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS:
            msg = "Jelly-RDF 1.2 streams cannot be of the GRAPHS physical type"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if options.stream_type not in (
            jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT,
            jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES,
        ):
            msg = f"unknown stream type: {options.stream_type}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        if options.rdf_version not in _RDF_VERSIONS:
            msg = f"unknown RDF version: {options.rdf_version}"
            raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
        min_names = MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE
    _check_size("name", options.max_name_table_size, min_names, MAX_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE)
    _check_size("prefix", options.max_prefix_table_size, 0, MAX_PREFIX_LOOKUP_SIZE)
    _check_size(
        "datatype", options.max_datatype_table_size, 0, MAX_DATATYPE_LOOKUP_SIZE
    )

def messages(rows: Iterable[Iterable[Any]]) -> Iterator[list[Any]]:
    """
    Group the rows of a stream of RDF Messages by message.

    message: list[Any] = []

                yield message
                message = []
            else:
                message.append(row)

def flat_rows(rows: Iterable[Iterable[Any]], options: ParserOptions) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """
    Return the rows of all frames, without the ends of RDF Messages.

    Args:
        rows (Iterable[Iterable[Any]]): the rows that Decoder.iter_rows() returns
            for each frame, and Decoder.end_of_stream()
        options (ParserOptions): the stream's options

    """
    # Not a generator: the rows of the frames reach the caller without passing
    # through one more Python frame
    all_rows = chain.from_iterable(rows)
    if options.params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES:
        return filter(partial(is_not, MESSAGE_END), all_rows)
    return all_rows

def add_value(self, term: EncodedTerm) -> None:
    """Add a run value: a term that is not the same as the one before."""
    kind = _kind_of(term)
    bit = 1 << kind
    used = self.kinds_used
    if used != bit:
        if not used & bit:
            self._new_kind(kind, used)
        kinds = self.kinds
        if kinds is not None:
            shift = (self.value_count & 3) << 1
            if shift:
                kinds[-1] |= kind << shift
            else:
                kinds.append(kind)
    self.value_count += 1
    if kind == KIND_IRI:
        self._add_iri(term.first, term.second)
    elif kind == KIND_LITERAL:
        self._add_literal(term)
    elif kind == KIND_BNODE:
        self.bnodes.append(term.text)
    else:
        assert term.triple_term is not None
        self.triple_terms.append(term.triple_term)

def write(self, batch: jelly.RdfColumnBatch) -> None:
    """Write the frame's statements into its batch, and start the next frame."""
    encoder = self.encoder
    batch.row_count = self.row_count
    encoder.names.packed.write(batch.names)
    encoder.prefixes.packed.write(batch.prefixes)
    encoder.datatypes.packed.write(batch.datatypes)
    for name, prefix_index, name_index in self.namespaces:
        declaration = batch.namespaces.add()
        declaration.name = name
        declaration.value.prefix_id = prefix_index
        declaration.value.name_id = name_index
    if self.row_count:
        self.subjects.write(batch.subjects)
        self.predicates.write(batch.predicates)
        self.objects.write(batch.objects)
        graphs = self.graphs
        if graphs is not None:
            if graphs.value_count:
                graphs.write(batch.graphs)
            else:
                # All statements are in the default graph: no column at all
                graphs.clear()
    if self.message_lengths:
        batch.message_lengths.extend(self.message_lengths)
    self.row_count = 0
    self.rows_in_messages = 0
    self.message_lengths = []
    self.namespaces = []
    self.new_frame()

def to_stream_frame(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Return the current frame, and start a new one.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame, None if it is empty

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is not None and batch.has_content():
        batch.write(self.frame.columns)
    elif not len(self.rows):
        return None
    frame = self.frame
    self.frame = jelly.RdfStreamFrame()
    self.rows = self.frame.rows
    return frame

def stream_type_for(
    params: StreamParameters, logical_type: jelly.LogicalStreamType
) -> jelly.RdfStreamType:
    """
    Return the Jelly-RDF 1.2 stream type of a stream that is written.

    As in Jelly-JVM, a stream of graphs or datasets (the logical types GRAPHS and
    DATASETS, and their subtypes) is a stream of RDF Messages, one per graph or
    dataset.

    >>> stream_type_for(StreamParameters(), jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES)
    0
    >>> stream_type_for(StreamParameters(), jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_NAMED_GRAPHS)
    1
    """
    if params.stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES or logical_type % 10 in (
        jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS,
        jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_DATASETS,
    ):
        return jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES
    return jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT

Abstract base class for producing Jelly frames from RDF stream rows.

Rows are added straight into the frame being built (see new_row()), so they never have to be copied: protobuf copies a message by serializing it and parsing it again.

In Jelly-RDF 1.2 streams, the frame's statements are in its column batch (see batch), and the rows only store the stream options. A frame may then also end because the lookups are full.

Allows for passing LogicalStreamType, required for logical subtypes and non-delimited streams.

def to_stream_frame(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Return the current frame, and start a new one.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame, None if it is empty

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is not None and batch.has_content():
        batch.write(self.frame.columns)
    elif not len(self.rows):
        return None
    frame = self.frame
    self.frame = jelly.RdfStreamFrame()
    self.rows = self.frame.rows
    return frame

def frame_from_bounds(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Emit frame from flow if full.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is None:
        if len(self.rows) >= self.frame_size:
            return self.to_stream_frame()
    elif batch.row_count >= self.frame_size or not batch.has_room():
        return self.to_stream_frame()
    return None

def flow_for_type(logical_type: jelly.LogicalStreamType) -> type[FrameFlow]:
    """
    Return flow based on logical type requested.

    Note: uses base logical type for subtypes (i.e., SUBJECT_GRAPHS uses
        the same flow as its base type GRAPHS).

    Args:
        logical_type (jelly.LogicalStreamType): logical type requested.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if (base) logical stream type is not supported.

    Returns:
        type[FrameFlow]: FrameFlow for respective logical type.

    """
    try:
        base_logical_type_value = logical_type % 10
        base_name = jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(base_logical_type_value)
        return FLOW_DISPATCH[getattr(jelly.LogicalStreamType, base_name)]
    except KeyError:
        msg = (
            "unsupported logical stream type: "
            f"{jelly.LogicalStreamType.Name(logical_type)}"
        )
        raise NotImplementedError(msg) from None

def column_batch(self, params: StreamParameters) -> ColumnBatch:
    """Set the stream up to write Jelly-RDF 1.2, and return its column batch."""
    max_names = self.options.lookup_preset.max_names
    if max_names < MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE:
        msg = (
            f"the name lookup size is {max_names}, but in Jelly-RDF 1.2 it must "
            f"be at least {MIN_COLUMN_NAME_LOOKUP_SIZE}"
        )
        raise JellyConformanceError(msg)
    encoder = self.encoder
    encoder.column_layout = True
    encoder.rdf_version = params.rdf_version
    stream_type = stream_type_for(params, self.stream_types.logical_type)
    batch = ColumnBatch(
        encoder,
        quads=self.physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_QUADS,
        messages=stream_type == jelly.RDF_STREAM_TYPE_MESSAGES,
    )
    self.flow.batch = batch
    return batch

def infer_flow(self) -> FrameFlow:
    """
    Return flow based on the stream options provided.

    Returns:
        FrameFlow: initialised FrameFlow object.

    """
    flow: FrameFlow
    if self.options.params.delimited:
        if self.options.logical_type != jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED:
            flow_class = flow_for_type(self.options.logical_type)
        else:
            flow_class = self.default_delimited_flow_class

        if issubclass(flow_class, BoundedFrameFlow) and (
            self.options.logical_type
            in (
                jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_TRIPLES,
                jelly.LOGICAL_STREAM_TYPE_FLAT_QUADS,
            )
        ):
            flow = flow_class(
                logical_type=self.options.logical_type,
                frame_size=self.options.frame_size,
            )
        else:
            flow = flow_class(logical_type=self.options.logical_type)
    else:
        flow = ManualFrameFlow(logical_type=self.options.logical_type)
    return flow

def encode_changed_spo(self) -> int:
    """
    Encode the subject, predicate and object that were set since the last emit.

    They are encoded in this order no matter in which order they were set:
    IRIs are encoded relative to the IRI before them, in the order the parser
    reads them. Rows for new lookup entries are added to the flow.

    Returns:
        int: which of them were encoded, as bits 0 (subject) to 2 (object).

    """
    terms = self.repeated_terms
    encoded = self.encoder.encoded
    changed = 0
    if self.subject_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_spo(terms[0], encoded[0])
        self.subject_changed = False
        changed = 1
    if self.predicate_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_spo(terms[1], encoded[1])
        self.predicate_changed = False
        changed |= 2
    if self.object_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_spo(terms[2], encoded[2])
        self.object_changed = False
        changed |= 4
    return changed

def write_changed_spo(self, statement: Statement, changed: int) -> None:
    """Write the terms encoded by encode_changed_spo() into the statement."""
    encoded = self.encoder.encoded
    if not changed:
        # Every term is repeated: the row is an empty statement
        statement.SetInParent()
    if changed & 1:
        write_term(encoded[0], statement, 0)
    if changed & 2:
        write_term(encoded[1], statement, 1)
    if changed & 4:
        write_term(encoded[2], statement, 2)

def for_rdflib(cls, options: SerializerOptions | None = None) -> Stream:
    """
    Initialize stream with RDFLib encoder.

    Args:
        options (SerializerOptions | None, optional): Stream options.
            Defaults to None.

    Raises:
        TypeError: if Stream is passed, and not a Stream for specific physical type.

    Returns:
        Stream: initialized stream with RDFLib encoder.

    """
    if cls is Stream:
        msg = "Stream is an abstract base class, use a subclass instead"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.encode import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        RDFLibTermEncoder,
    )

    lookup_preset: LookupPreset | None = None
    if options is not None:
        lookup_preset = options.lookup_preset
    return cls(
        encoder=RDFLibTermEncoder(lookup_preset=lookup_preset),
        options=options,
    )

def emit(self) -> jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None:
    """
    Add a quad made of the terms set with the cursor API.

    Returns:
        jelly.RdfStreamFrame | None: stream frame if
            flow supports frames slicing and current flow is full

    """
    batch = self.batch
    if batch is not None:
        self.add_changed_spo(batch)
        batch.add_graph_changed(self.repeated_terms[3], changed=self.graph_changed)
        self.graph_changed = False
        batch.row_count += 1
        return self.flow.frame_from_bounds()
    self.encoder.new_epoch()
    # The terms first, as they add rows for new lookup entries. The graph
    # comes last, as in the parser.
    changed = self.encode_changed_spo()
    graph_changed = self.graph_changed
    if graph_changed:
        self.encoder.encode_graph(self.repeated_terms[3], self.encoder.encoded[3])
        self.graph_changed = False
        changed |= 8
    quad = self.flow.new_row().quad
    self.write_changed_spo(quad, changed)
    if graph_changed:
        write_graph(self.encoder.encoded[3], quad)
    return self.flow.frame_from_bounds()

def stream_for_type(physical_type: jelly.PhysicalStreamType) -> type[Stream]:
    """
    Give a Stream based on physical type specified.

    Args:
        physical_type (jelly.PhysicalStreamType): jelly stream physical type.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: if no stream for requested physical type is available.

    Returns:
        type[Stream]: jelly stream

    """
    try:
        stream_cls = STREAM_DISPATCH[physical_type]
    except KeyError:
        if physical_type == jelly.PHYSICAL_STREAM_TYPE_GRAPHS:
            msg = (
                "writing streams of the GRAPHS physical type is not supported "
                "(they can still be read). Use QUADS instead."
            )
        else:
            msg = (
                "no stream class for physical type "
                f"{jelly.PhysicalStreamType.Name(physical_type)}"
            )
        raise NotImplementedError(msg) from None
    return stream_cls

docs.text: This guide explains how to use pyjelly’s generic API to write and read RDF statements into the Jelly format without any external library.

pip install pyjelly

docs.title: Usage without external libraries
docs.text: Unlike the example in getting started, the Generic API does not use the RDFLib or any other third-party libraries, but it works in much the same way.

docs.title: Serializing statements to a Jelly file
docs.text:
To make a set of triples/quads and write them to a Jelly file, use:

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.generic_sink import *

# Create a generic sink object
generic_sink = GenericStatementSink()

# Let's add triples one by one
generic_sink.add(
    Triple(
        IRI("http://example.com/subject"),
        IRI("http://example.com/predicate"),
        Literal("Hello", langtag="en"),
    )
)
generic_sink.add(
    Triple(
        BlankNode("B1"),
        IRI("http://example.com/hasName"),
        Literal("Bob"),
    )
)

# Write into a Jelly file
with open("output.jelly", "wb") as out_file:
    generic_sink.serialize(out_file)

print("All done.")

This example uses pyjelly’s simple custom triple/quad type, which is easy to create and work with.

# Create a generic sink object
generic_sink = GenericStatementSink()

# Load triples from the Jelly file
with open("output.jelly", "rb") as in_file:
    generic_sink.parse(in_file)

# Let's inspect them statement by statement
for statement in generic_sink:
    if isinstance(statement, Triple):
        print(statement)

print("All done.")

Which retrieves data from your .jelly file.

docs.title: Parsing a stream of graphs
docs.text:
Similarly, to process a Jelly stream as a stream of graphs through generic API, see:

import gzip
import urllib.request

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.parse import parse_jelly_grouped

# Dataset: Katrina weather measurements (10k graphs)
# Documentation: https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/lod-katrina/dev
url = "https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/lod-katrina/dev/files/jelly_10K.jelly.gz"

# Load, uncompress .gz file, and pass to Jelly parser, all in a streaming manner
with (
    urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response,
    gzip.open(response) as jelly_stream,
):
    # Parse into sinks (one per graph)
    graphs = parse_jelly_grouped(jelly_stream)

    # First 50
    for i, graph in enumerate(graphs):
        print(f"Graph {i} in the stream has {len(graph)} triples")
        if i >= 50:
            break

Where we use a dataset of weather measurements and count the number of triples in each graph.

docs.title: Parsing a stream of statements
docs.text:
You can also process a Jelly stream as a flat stream with only generic API:

We look through a fragment of Denmark's OpenStreetMap to find all city names:

import gzip
import urllib.request

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.generic_sink import *
from pyjelly.integrations.generic.parse import parse_jelly_flat

# Dataset: OpenStreetMap data for Denmark (first 10k objects)
# Documentation: https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/osm2rdf-denmark/dev
url = (
    "https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/osm2rdf-denmark/dev/files/jelly_10K.jelly.gz"
)

# We are looking for city names in the dataset
predicate_to_look_for = IRI("https://www.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:addr:city")
city_names = set()

with (
    urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response,
    gzip.open(response) as jelly_stream,
):
    for event in parse_jelly_flat(jelly_stream):
        if isinstance(event, Triple):
            if str(event.p) == str(predicate_to_look_for):
                city_names.add(str(event.o))

print(f"Found {len(city_names)} unique city names in the dataset.")
print("Sample city names:")
for city in list(city_names)[:10]:
    print(f"- {city}")

We get a generator of stream events, which allows us to process the file statement-by-statement, however with no external libraries used.

docs.title: Streaming data
docs.text:
If you need to process a certain quantity of statements both efficiently and iteratively, you can provide a simple generator:

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.generic_sink import *


# Helper generator that streams statements from a Jelly file path
def stream_triples(jelly_path):
    generic_sink = GenericStatementSink()
    with open(jelly_path, "rb") as f:
        generic_sink.parse(f)
    yield from (stmt for stmt in generic_sink)


# Example usage, just printing:
for triple in stream_triples("output.jelly"):
    print(triple)

print("All done.")

With this method you avoid storing all statements in memory, which greatly improves performance.

docs.title: Serializing a stream of graphs
docs.text:
If you have a generator object containing graphs, you can use a generic approach for serialization:

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.generic_sink import *
from pyjelly.integrations.generic.serialize import grouped_stream_to_file
import random


# Helper function to generate a generator of graphs
def generate_sample_sinks():
    content = (
        IRI("http://example.com/sensor"),
        IRI("http://example.com/humidity"),
        IRI(f"http://example.com/{random.random()}"),
    )
    for _ in range(10):
        sink = GenericStatementSink()
        sink.add(Triple(*content))
        yield sink


output_file = "output.jelly"
print(f"Streaming graphs into {output_file}…")
with open(output_file, "wb") as out_f:
    grouped_stream_to_file(generate_sample_sinks(), out_f)
print("All done.")

Grouped data is streamed in its original form, no need for additional RDF libraries like RDFLib.

docs.title: Serializing a stream of statements
docs.text:
Serializing a generator object of statements to .jelly file through generic API:

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.serialize import flat_stream_to_file
from pyjelly.integrations.generic.generic_sink import *
import random


# Example generator that yields raw triples
def generate_sample_triples():
    content = (
        IRI("http://example.com/sensor"),
        IRI("http://example.com/humidity"),
        IRI(f"http://example.com/{random.random()}"),
    )
    for _ in range(10):
        yield Triple(*content)


output_file = "flat_output.jelly"
print(f"Streaming triples into {output_file}…")
sample_triples = generate_sample_triples()
with open(output_file, "wb") as out_f:
    flat_stream_to_file(sample_triples, out_f)
print("All done.")

Data is transmitted and kept ordered and simple.

docs.title: Working with byte buffers and Kafka
docs.text:
When working with Kafka or other message brokers, you may want to write Jelly data to a byte buffer instead of a file. You can do this by using the BytesIO class from the io module:

import io

from pyjelly.integrations.generic.generic_sink import *

g1 = GenericStatementSink()

g1.add(
    Triple(
        IRI("http://example.com/subject"),
        IRI("http://example.com/predicate"),
        Literal("Hello", langtag="en"),
    )
)

# Write the data into a byte buffer (bytes type)
with io.BytesIO() as write_buffer:
    g1.serialize(write_buffer)
    data = write_buffer.getvalue()

print(f"Serialized data size: {len(data)} bytes")

# Parse the data back
g2 = GenericStatementSink()
with io.BytesIO(data) as read_buffer:
    g2.parse(read_buffer)

print("\nParsed triples:")
for statement in g2:
    print(statement)

The data variable is of type bytes, and can be passed to Kafka with KafkaProducer.send(value=data), or any other API that accepts byte buffers. Same trick may be used when working with the RDFLib integration.

When working with Kafka, you should be aware of the broker's offset management and partitioning strategies. Data within one Jelly stream must be strictly ordered and no frames may be dropped. If you have less strict ordering guarantees, you should split up the stream into multiple Jelly streams, each with guaranteed consistency.

docs.title: Accessing stream frame metadata
docs.text:
It is possible to access RdfStreamFrame metadata in pyjelly via context variables. To do that, define a context variable before parsing and pass it as argument to parser functions, e.g.:

from contextvars import ContextVar
from google.protobuf.internal.containers import ScalarMap
import urllib.request
from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.parse import parse_jelly_grouped

frame_metadata: ContextVar[ScalarMap[str, bytes]] = ContextVar("frame_metadata")

url = "https://registry.petapico.org/nanopubs.jelly"
with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response:
    graphs = parse_jelly_grouped(response, frame_metadata=frame_metadata)
    for i, graph in enumerate(graphs):
        if i == 1:  # Just show first instance
            break
        print(f"Graph {i} in the stream has {len(graph)} triples.")
        metadata = frame_metadata.get()
        print(f"Graph #{i}: {metadata}")

docs.text: If you are familiar with RDFLib, you can use pyjelly together with RDFLib in a similar way. See the dedicated guide.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing and working with pyjelly and RDFLib.

docs.title: Installation (with RDFLib)
docs.text:
Install pyjelly from PyPI:

pip install pyjelly[rdflib]

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer
  • Linux, macOS, or Windows

docs.title: Usage with RDFLib
docs.text: Once you install pyjelly, it integrates automatically with RDFLib through standard RDFLib API.

docs.title: Serializing a graph
docs.text:
To serialize a graph to the Jelly format see:

from rdflib import Graph

g = Graph()
g.parse("https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/integrated/examples/sunspots.ttl")
g.serialize(destination="foaf.jelly", format="jelly")

This creates a delimited Jelly stream using default options.

docs.title: Including namespace declarations (prefixes)
docs.text:
By default, Jelly serializes only triples/quads. To also include namespace declarations (prefixes) in the output, enable the namespace_declarations option. Prefixes bound in RDFLib's namespace manager will then be written into the Jelly stream and restored on parsing.

from rdflib import Graph, Namespace, URIRef, Literal
from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.serialize import SerializerOptions, StreamParameters

# Build a tiny graph and bind a prefix
g = Graph()
EX = Namespace("http://example.org/")
g.namespace_manager.bind("ex", EX)
g.add((EX.alice, URIRef("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name"), Literal("Alice")))

print("IN  namespaces:", dict(g.namespaces()))

# Enable namespace declarations in Jelly output
options = SerializerOptions(params=StreamParameters(namespace_declarations=True))

# Serialize with options
g.serialize("sample_test.jelly", format="jelly", options=options)

# Parse back and check namespaces
g_new = Graph()
g_new.parse("sample_test.jelly", format="jelly")
print("OUT namespaces:", dict(g_new.namespaces()))

Tip

For an existing graph you can (re)bind a prefix just before saving:

g.namespace_manager.bind("ex", EX, replace=True)

docs.title: Parsing a graph
docs.text:
To load RDF data from a .jelly file see:

from rdflib import Graph

g = Graph()
g.parse("foaf.jelly", format="jelly")

print("Parsed triples:")
for s, p, o in g:
    print(f"{s} {p} {o}")

RDFLib will reconstruct the graph from the Jelly file.

docs.title: Parsing a stream of graphs
docs.text:
You can process a Jelly stream as a stream of graphs. A Jelly file consists of "frames" (batches of statements) – we can load each frame as a separate RDFLib graph.

In this example, we use a dataset of weather measurements. We count the number of triples in each graph:

import gzip
import urllib.request

from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.parse import parse_jelly_grouped

# Dataset: Katrina weather measurements (10k graphs)
# Documentation: https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/lod-katrina/dev
url = "https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/lod-katrina/dev/files/jelly_10K.jelly.gz"

# Load, uncompress .gz file, and pass to Jelly parser, all in a streaming manner
with (
    urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response,
    gzip.open(response) as jelly_stream,
):
    graphs = parse_jelly_grouped(jelly_stream)
    for i, graph in enumerate(graphs):
        print(f"Graph {i} in the stream has {len(graph)} triples")
        # Limit to 50 graphs for demonstration -- the rest will not be parsed
        if i >= 50:
            break

Each iteration receives only one graph, allowing for processing large datasets efficiently, without exhausting memory.

docs.title: Parsing a stream of triples
docs.text:
You can also process a Jelly stream as a flat stream of triples.

We look through a fragment of Denmark's OpenStreetMap to find all city names:

import gzip
import urllib.request

from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.parse import parse_jelly_flat
from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.statements import Triple
from rdflib import URIRef

# Dataset: OpenStreetMap data for Denmark (first 10k objects)
# Documentation: https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/osm2rdf-denmark/dev
url = (
    "https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/osm2rdf-denmark/dev/files/jelly_10K.jelly.gz"
)

# We are looking for city names in the dataset
predicate_to_look_for = URIRef("https://www.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:addr:city")
city_names = set()

with (
    urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response,
    gzip.open(response) as jelly_stream,
):
    for event in parse_jelly_flat(jelly_stream):
        if isinstance(event, Triple):  # we are only interested in triples
            if event.p == predicate_to_look_for:
                city_names.add(event.o)

print(f"Found {len(city_names)} unique city names in the dataset.")
print("10 random city names:")
for city in list(city_names)[:10]:
    print(f"- {city}")

parse_jelly_flat returns a generator of stream events (i.e., statements parsed). This case allows you to efficiently process the file triple-by-triple and build custom aggregations from the stream.

docs.title: Checking IRIs
docs.text: By default, the IRIs in a Jelly file are not checked when it is read into RDFLib, which makes reading faster. To turn it on, set validate_iris=True, e.g., graph.parse("data.jelly", format="jelly", validate_iris=True). The parsing functions in pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.parse take the same argument.

docs.title: Serializing a stream of graphs
docs.text:
If you have a generator object containing graphs, you can easily serialize it into the Jelly format: 

from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.serialize import grouped_stream_to_file

from rdflib import Graph, Literal, Namespace
import random


def generate_sample_graphs():
    ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
    for _ in range(10):
        g = Graph()
        g.add((ex.sensor, ex.temperature, Literal(random.random())))
        g.add((ex.sensor, ex.humidity, Literal(random.random())))
        yield g


output_file_name = "output.jelly"

print(f"Streaming graphs into {output_file_name}…")
sample_graphs = generate_sample_graphs()
with open(output_file_name, "wb") as out_file:
    grouped_stream_to_file(sample_graphs, out_file)
print("All done.")

This method allows for transmitting logically grouped data, preserving their original division: each graph is one RDF Message. For more precise control over frame serialization you can use lower-level API

docs.title: Serializing a stream of statements
docs.text:
If you have a generator object containing statements, you can easily serialize it into the Jelly format: 

from pyjelly.integrations.rdflib.serialize import flat_stream_to_file
from rdflib import Literal, Namespace
import random


# example generator with triples statements
def generate_sample_triples():
    ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
    for _ in range(10):
        yield (ex.sensor, ex.temperature, Literal(random.random()))


output_file_name = "flat_output.jelly"

print(f"Streaming triples into {output_file_name}…")
sample_triples = generate_sample_triples()
with open(output_file_name, "wb") as out_file:
    flat_stream_to_file(sample_triples, out_file)
print("All done.")

The flat method transmits the data as a continuous sequence of statements, keeping it simple and ordered. For more precise control over frame serialization you can use lower-level API

docs.title: File extension support
docs.text:
You can generally omit the format="jelly" parameter if the file ends in .jelly – RDFLib will auto-detect the format:

from rdflib import Graph
import pyjelly.integrations.rdflib

g = Graph()
g.parse("foaf.jelly")

Warning

Unfortunately, the way this is implemented in RDFLib is a bit wonky, so it will only work if you explicitly import pyjelly.integrations.rdflib, or you used format="jelly" in the serialize() or parse() call before.

docs.title: NetworkX
docs.text:
NetworkX is a Python package that represents complex networks as graphs and allows for their manipulation.

Install the following libraries:

pip install pyjelly[rdflib] networkx==3.2.1 matplotlib==3.9.4

Below there are few useful examples to follow.

docs.title: Parse graph, show it
docs.text:
Let's investigate relationships between worldwide political figures (support and opposition relations)! We are given a graph in .jelly containing information about political stances extracted from news articles. Let's dive in and get some useful information!

We can easily load it: 

# Parse RDF from the Jelly format
rdf_g = Graph()
rdf_g.parse(example_file, format="jelly")
print(f"Loaded graph with {len(rdf_g)} instances.")

Output from print():

Loaded graph with 90000 instances.

Convert it into a convenient NetworkX graph:

# Convert to a NetworkX graph
nx_g = rdflib_to_networkx_graph(rdf_g_filtered)

Is our graph fully connected? It's important to know (are all political relations tied together?), let's check here:

# Example calculation, get the number of connected components in a graph
num_components = nx.number_connected_components(nx_g)
print(f"Connected components: {num_components}")

Output from print():

Connected components: 24

Which nodes are connected the most (have most connections?), let's see top 5 of them:

# Example calculation, get top 5 objects with highest degrees, simple in NetworkX
top5 = sorted(nx_g.degree, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:5]
print("Top 5 nodes sorted by degree:")
for node, deg in top5:
    print(f"{node}: {deg}")

Output from print():

Top 5 nodes sorted by degree:
Socrates: 241
Cavaco: 189
Passos Coelho: 187
Costa: 179
Antonio Costa: 168

What is the shortest path between two nodes? We can check:

target = next(n for n in nx_g if norm(n) == "obama")
path = nx.shortest_path(nx_g, source=source, target=target)
print(f"Shortest path from {source} to {target}: {' -> '.join(path)}")

# Take first 10 nodes

Output from print():

Shortest path from Socrates to Obama: Socrates -> Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa -> Durao Barroso -> Obama

However, it's best to see the full picture (for our example we truncate to 10 nodes for clarity):

subg = nx_g.subgraph(nodes)

# Draw and display the graph
pos_sub = nx.spring_layout(subg, k=5, iterations=200, scale=3, seed=24)
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))

# Introduce your own settings for display
nx.draw_networkx(subg, pos_sub, font_size=14, node_size=220, linewidths=0.7)
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

print("All done.")

The graph presents as follows

In summary:

Entire example 
import urllib.request, gzip, tempfile, shutil, os

import networkx as nx
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from rdflib import Graph, URIRef, BNode, Literal
from rdflib.extras.external_graph_libs import rdflib_to_networkx_graph

# Filter predicates for people
TARGET_PREDICATES = {
    URIRef("http://www.politiquices.pt/ent2_str"),
    URIRef("http://www.politiquices.pt/ent1_str"),
}

# URL to the dataset
url = "https://w3id.org/riverbench/datasets/politiquices/1.0.3/files/jelly_10K.jelly.gz"

# Load example jelly file
with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as r:
    fd, example_file = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".jelly")
    os.close(fd)
    with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=r) as g, open(example_file, "wb") as out:
        shutil.copyfileobj(g, out)

# Parse RDF from the Jelly format
rdf_g = Graph()
rdf_g.parse(example_file, format="jelly")
print(f"Loaded graph with {len(rdf_g)} instances.")

# First step for filtering the graph
rdf_g_filtered = Graph()
for s, p, o in rdf_g.triples((None, None, None)):
    if p in TARGET_PREDICATES:
        rdf_g_filtered.add((s, p, o))

# Just filtering the graph for clarity of visualization, can be omitted
related = URIRef("http://www.politiquices.pt/related")
for b in list(rdf_g_filtered.subjects()):
    if isinstance(b, BNode):
        ent1 = ent2 = None
        for p, o in rdf_g_filtered.predicate_objects(b):
            if p == URIRef("http://www.politiquices.pt/ent1_str") and isinstance(
                o, Literal
            ):
                ent1 = o
            elif p == URIRef("http://www.politiquices.pt/ent2_str") and isinstance(
                o, Literal
            ):
                ent2 = o
        if ent1 and ent2:
            rdf_g_filtered.add((ent1, related, ent2))
            rdf_g_filtered.add((ent2, related, ent1))
        for triple in list(rdf_g_filtered.triples((b, None, None))):
            rdf_g_filtered.remove(triple)

# Convert to a NetworkX graph
nx_g = rdflib_to_networkx_graph(rdf_g_filtered)

# Example calculation, get the number of connected components in a graph
num_components = nx.number_connected_components(nx_g)
print(f"Connected components: {num_components}")

# Example calculation, get top 5 objects with highest degrees, simple in NetworkX
top5 = sorted(nx_g.degree, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:5]
print("Top 5 nodes sorted by degree:")
for node, deg in top5:
    print(f"{node}: {deg}")

# Helper function
norm = lambda n: (
    str(n.value).strip().lower() if isinstance(n, Literal) else str(n).strip().lower()
)

# Example calculation, shortest path between two nodes (provided at least two nodes)
source = next(n for n in nx_g if norm(n) == "socrates")
target = next(n for n in nx_g if norm(n) == "obama")
path = nx.shortest_path(nx_g, source=source, target=target)
print(f"Shortest path from {source} to {target}: {' -> '.join(path)}")

# Take first 10 nodes
nodes = list(nx_g)[:10]
subg = nx_g.subgraph(nodes)

# Draw and display the graph
pos_sub = nx.spring_layout(subg, k=5, iterations=200, scale=3, seed=24)
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))

# Introduce your own settings for display
nx.draw_networkx(subg, pos_sub, font_size=14, node_size=220, linewidths=0.7)
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

print("All done.")

We converted an RDFLib graph to NetworkX, calculated insightful metrics and visualized the graph.

For more info about the data source please see the Politiquices dataset in RiverBench and its original source (Portuguese).

docs.title: Serialize NetworkX graph
docs.text:
This example shows how to write a NetworkX graph to a Jelly file.:

import networkx as nx
from rdflib import Graph, URIRef, Namespace
from rdflib.namespace import RDF

# An example NetworkX graph
nx_g = nx.Graph()
nx_g.add_node("http://example.org/A")
nx_g.add_node("http://example.org/B")
nx_g.add_edge("http://example.org/A", "http://example.org/B")

# We define RDFLib graph for further conversion
rdf_g = Graph()

# Example namespace
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/ns#")

# Add triples through node information in NetworkX graph
for node_uri, data in nx_g.nodes(data=True):
    subj = URIRef(node_uri)
    rdf_g.add((subj, RDF.type, ex.Node))

# Add triples through edge information in NetworkX graph
for u, v, attr in nx_g.edges(data=True):
    rdf_g.add((URIRef(u), ex.connectedTo, URIRef(v)))

# Serialize graph into a .jelly file
rdf_g.serialize(destination="networkx_graph.jelly", format="jelly")
print("All done.")

Which converts the NetworkX graph into an RDFLib Graph instance and serializes it.
